rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The weakened أن has an omitted pronoun and means أنه; Elmalılı reads the clause as divine speech coordinated to 72:1, not as the jinns’ speech.
rows.anchor: اَنَّهُ demektir ve bu cinlerin kelâmından değil أَنَّهُ ٱسْتَمَعَ’ya ma‘tuf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If jinn and humans all kept to the path of faith and Islam, God would give them abundant water, meaning plentiful provision.
rows.anchor: o iman ve islâm yolunda bir tarîkat üzere dosdoğru gitselerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This world is a place of testing, and both scarcity and abundance are trials.
rows.anchor: Bu âlem, imtihan âlemi olduğu için bunun darlığı da genişliği de bir imtihandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the steadfast, God would test them through plentiful provision rather than hardship and thereby raise them.
rows.anchor: Onun için onlar o istikāmetle gitselerdi onları darlıklar içinde değil, bol bol rızıklar içinde imtihan eder, o yüzden yükseltirdik.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away from the Lord’s reminder, revelation, counsel, or worship brings a punishment that rises progressively.
rows.anchor: Her kim de Rabbinin zikrinden, vahy ü nasihatinden, ibadetinden i‘râz ederse O onu gittikçe yükselen bir azâba sokar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is read with fatḥ in every reading and connected to the preceding conditional clause; mosques belong to God, so worship is for God alone.
rows.anchor: Bu da kıraatlerin hepsinde meftuhtur. اَنْ لَو gibi yukarıya ma‘tuftur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mesâcid is normally the plural of mescid, though it can also be the plural of mesced with fatḥ on the jīm.
rows.anchor: “Mesâcid” mâlum olduğu üzere “mescid”in cem‘idir. Cîm’in fethiyle “mesced”in cem‘i de olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra, mescid means a place designated for prostration, prayer, and worship; lexically it covers every community’s worship place, while conventionally it means a Muslim mosque.
rows.anchor: olan yerlerdir ki lügaten müslim ve gayr-i müslim her milletin mâbedine şâmil olabilir. Örfte ehl-i islâmın mâbedine mahsustur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kasra form is an exceptional place-noun pattern that distinguishes a mosque from the regular morphological pattern.
rows.anchor: İmtiyâzına tenbih için ism-i mekânın şâz vezinlerinden olmak üzere meksur okunarak kıyastan ayırt edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥ, mesced can be a verbal noun for prostration, or a regular place noun for the place or bodily part of prostration.
rows.anchor: Cîm’in fethiyle “mesced” ise secde mânasına mimli masdar veya secde mevzii, secde uzvu mânasına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites a Prophetic report that he was commanded to prostrate on seven limbs, which he identifies as forehead and nose, hands, knees, and feet.
rows.anchor: أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَسْجُدَ عَلَى سَبـْعَةِ آرَابٍ “Yedi a‘zâ üzerine secde ile emr olundum”[^29] hadîsinde beyan olunduğu üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent and majority interpretation is worship places generally, as in 2:114; Jews and Christians also invoke others in synagogues and churches, so Muslims are commanded to worship sincerely.
rows.anchor: burada da zâhir olan evvelki mâna ile ibadethânelerdir, cumhûrun kavli de budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Muslim-specific mosques had not yet been built when this surah was revealed, Elmalılı also considers broader interpretations of mesâcid.
rows.anchor: Ancak bu sûre nâzil olduğu zaman Müslümanlara mahsus mescidler yapılmış olmadığı için

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says the whole earth was made a mosque and purifier; Hasan al-Basri uses it to support a broad reading.
rows.anchor: جُعِلَتْ لِيَ الأَْرْضُ مَسْجِدًا طَهُورًا

rows.speaker: حسن البصري
rows.claim: Hasan al-Basri takes mesâcid to mean all regions of the earth: since the earth belongs to its Creator, no one should prostrate on it to another.
rows.anchor: Hasan-ı Basrî demiştir ki: “Burada ‘mesâcid’[^31], Arz’ın bütün buk‘alarına işarettir.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes mesced as the verbal noun for prostrations, meaning that prayers belong to God and one must not prostrate to anyone else.
rows.anchor: Yahut “mesced” feth ile mimli masdar olmak üzere “secdeler, yani namazlar Allah’a mahsustur; başkasına secde etmeyin” demektir.

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the prostrating limbs are God’s creatures, so they must not be used to prostrate to anyone besides God.
rows.anchor: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr de demiştir ki: “Secde a‘zâları olan mescedler Allah’ındır, yani Allah’ın mahlûkudur.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas, transmitted by Ata, identifies mesâcid here specifically as the Sacred Mosque; because it contains many mosques, other mosques are covered by implication.
rows.anchor: Atâ, İbn Abbas’tan burada “mesâcid”den[^33] murad Mescid-i Haram’dır diye de bir rivayet söylemiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although each interpretation has a rationale, Elmalılı considers the majority’s general meaning, all houses of worship, the most apparent.
rows.anchor: en zâhir olan cumhûr-i ulemânın dediği vechile ale’l-umûm ibadethaneler demek olmasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase wa annahu is kasra for Nafiʿ and Abu Bakr from Asim, but fatḥ for Hafs and the other readings.
rows.anchor: Burada أَنَّهُ Nâfi‘ve Âsım’dan Ebû Bekir kıraatlerinde kesr ile, Hafs’ta vesâir kıraatlerin hepsinde feth ile okunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some connect the kasra reading to the jinns’ speech, but Elmalılı finds a divine resumptive clause more fitting because the intervening verse makes the connection less elegant.
rows.anchor: kesr kıraatinde vâv atıf olmayıp taraf-ı ilâhîden istînaf olması daha muvâfık olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥ reading attaches the clause to the revelation; on these readings, the subject of kādū may be the jinn or both jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: Feth[^37] ile okunması ise vahiy cümlesine atıftır. Bu suretlerde كَادُوا۟ zamiri cine veya cin ve inse ait olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abdullah means God’s servant, Muhammad; this title signals humility alongside his special devotion in fulfilling servitude to God.
rows.anchor: “Abdullah” Allah’ın kulu, bu vahiy kendisine indirilmiş olan Hazret-i Peygamber’in kendisidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading, the listening jinn crowded densely around the Prophet, almost piling together like felt, because his worship and prayer were unfamiliar to them.
rows.anchor: o dinleyen cinler ta‘cillerinden kesret ve izdiham ile etrafına öyle toplandılar ki az daha keçe gibi birbirlerine geçeceklerdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the passage is the jinns’ speech, it means hostile polytheists crowded around the Prophet while he prayed, nearly pressing together.
rows.anchor: Cinler kavimlerine şunu da söylediler: “O Allah’ın kulu kalkmış Allah’a dua ederken müşrik insanlar ona adâvetle aleyhine öyle toplanmışlardı

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada’s third interpretation is that unbelieving jinn and humans gathered against the Prophet to thwart his mission; God protects and grants him victory, and the view fits both readings and 72:13.
rows.anchor: Katâde’den mervî olan üçüncü bir mâna daha vardır. Şöyle ki: İns ü cin kâfirleri onun işini, kıyam ve davetini ibtal etmek için aleyhinde öyle toplanmışlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either way, the passage informs the Prophet of outward and inward events and feelings occurring beyond his presence.
rows.anchor: Ve her iki takdirde de Peygamber’e gıyâbında cereyan eden zâhirî ve bâtınî ahvâl ve hissiyâtı ihbardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the commands that follow fit the flow of these verses well.
rows.anchor: Bundan sonraki emirler, âyetlerin sevkiyle de gayet mütenâsibdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mefâz can be a verbal noun meaning victory or salvation, or a place noun meaning the place of victory.
rows.anchor: “Mefâz” fevz mânasına mimli masdar veya fevzgâh mânasına ism-i mekân olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fevz in its full sense combines escape from fear and pain with attaining one’s aims, though it can sometimes denote either alone.
rows.anchor: “Fevz” halâs ve zafer, yani korkulardan, acılardan kurtulup muradlara ermektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin signals grandeur: the verse promises great deliverance from eternal punishment and attainment of eternal bliss and reward.
rows.anchor: Tenvin tâzim içindir. Yani büyük kurtuluş büyük meram var, ki o ebedî azabdan halâs, ebedî na‘îm ve sevâba nâiliyettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mefâz is a great place of victory, namely the Garden of eternal bliss.
rows.anchor: Yahut büyük bir fevz yeri var ki o da dârü’n-na‘îm olan cennettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens are bounded orchards with water, varied fruit trees, and flowers; their name evokes the pupil of the eye by resemblance in appearance.
rows.anchor: suyu olan ve türlü meyve ağaçlarını ve çiçekleri hâvî ve etrafı duvar ile muhât bulunan bostan ve bahçe demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿnāb can mean grapes or grapevines.
rows.anchor: “A‘nâb” üzüme de üzüm bağlarına da denir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kawāʿib is the plural of kāʿib, referring to young girls whose breasts have newly rounded or developed.
rows.anchor: “Kâ‘ib”in[^3] cem‘i ki memeleri kübik, yani yeni ağırşaklanmış, turunç memeli denilen taze kızlara denir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atrab is the plural of tirb, meaning people of the same age; some commentaries report paradise women as sixteen and men as thirty-three.
rows.anchor: “Tirb”in cem‘i, hep bir yaşta. Bazı tefsirlerde cennet kızları hep on altı yaşında, erkekleri otuz üç yaşında diye mervîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dihāq means filled to the brim, with a link to 76:5.
rows.anchor: Dopdolu هَلْ اَتٰى sûresinde إِنَّ ٱلْأَبْرَارَ يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍۢ [el-İnsân 76/5] bak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hisāban means fully sufficient and complete reward: the righteous receive more than the wages for their deeds, in contrast to the tyrants’ exact recompense.
rows.anchor: tam kifayet mânasından yeter mi yeter deyinceye kadar kâfî ve vâfî meâlinde tefsir olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb of the heavens is grammatically appositional to “your Lord,” and al-Rahmān is an explanatory apposition.
rows.anchor: } رَّبِّكَ’den bedeldir. {ٱلرَّحْمَٰن} atf-ı beyan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement magnifies God’s sovereignty and independence in judgment and gift: no creature of heaven or earth can interfere or speak on God’s behalf without leave.
rows.anchor: bütün semâvât ve Arz sekenesi, yukarıda ve aşağıda bütün mahlûkāt fiilen O’nun işine müdahale etmek şöyle dursun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creatures cannot claim authority to address God on their own; if permitted, they speak as recipients of leave, not as owners of speech.
rows.anchor: O’nun nâmına kendiliklerinden bir söz söylemek veya O’na bir hitapta bulunmak salâhiyetine mâlik değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm yaqumu reinforces rather than restricts the meaning of la yamlikun; it may instead attach to la yatakallamun, but Elmalılı prefers taking it as a replacement for 78:18’s yawm yunfakhu.
rows.anchor: {يَوْمَ يَقُومُ} لَا يَمْلِكُونَ mazmûnunu takrirdir, takyid değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rūḥ first suggests the genus of spirits; a cited hadith calls the Spirit a troop of God and says they are not angels.
rows.anchor: “Rûh Allah’ın cünûdundan bir cünddür. Melâike değildirler. ilh”[^8] meâlinde rivayet olunan bir hadis

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the Spirit as the guardians among the angels; others say it is an angel charged with the spirits.
rows.anchor: Bazıları melâikenin hafazası demişler, bazıları da ervâh üzerine müvekkel melek demişler.

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Ghazali says in the Ihya that the angel called Spirit places souls into bodies through breathing, and that people of spiritual insight perceive this truth.
rows.anchor: Gazzâlî İhyâ’sında “rûh denilen melek, ervâhı ecsâma sokandır.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the Spirit as Gabriel, who stands trembling before God at resurrection and confesses that worshippers did not worship God as fully as due.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan rivayet olunan kavilde ise Cibrîl’dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-Rūḥ can be referential: because the Prophet is addressed by min rabbika, it means the Spirit already known to him.
rows.anchor: مِّن رَّبِّكَ karînesiyle muhatab Resûlullah olduğu cihetle onca ma‘hud olan rûh demek olur.

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Baydawi summarizes the possibilities as an angel charged with spirits, the class of spirits, Gabriel, or a great creation among the angels.
rows.anchor: Beyzâvî bunları şöyle telhîs eder: “Rûh, ervâh üzerine müvekkel bir melek veya ervâh cinsi yahut Cebrâil, yahut melâikeden a‘zam bir halktır.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı prefers affirming the general meaning while consigning the Spirit’s exact identity to God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde mazmûnuna iman edip tafsîline “el-ilmi indallah” demek daha muvâfık olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some take saffan as a single row, 89:22 shows that the Spirit and angels stand in rows upon rows.
rows.anchor: وَٱلْمَلَكُ صَفًّۭا صَفًّۭا [el-Fecr 89/22] saf saf olmasını anlatır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La yatakallamun is an independent sentence reaffirming la yamlikun; its pronoun could refer to the Spirit and angels, but the broader reference to all inhabitants of heaven and earth fits better.
rows.anchor: Cümle-i istînâfiye olarak لَا يَمْلِكُونَ mazmûnunu takrirdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one, including the Spirit, angels, or others, can speak for intercession, request, or any other purpose unless the Merciful permits.
rows.anchor: gerek Rûh ve gerek melâike ve gerek sâireden hiçbiri ne bir şefaat ne bir talep ne de herhangi bir maksad ile bir söz söyleyemezler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception allows only someone permitted by the Merciful who speaks correctly; such speech occurs by permission, not ownership.
rows.anchor: Ancak o Rahmân’ın izin verdiği savab söyleyen kimse müstesnâ o kimse izne iktiran etmek ve savab söylemek şartıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This exception opens the door to intercession: those near God may intercede, with Muhammad first authorized for universal intercession at the Praised Station, followed by particular intercessions.
rows.anchor: bu izin ile istisnâda şefaat kapısının bir küşâdı vardır. Makām-ı kurbda bulunanlar bu suretle şefaat edebileceklerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı’s first answer treats “speaking correctly” as a defining quality and first condition of intercession; because God’s approval is known only by His will, intercessors speak in fear and only sound intercession is accepted.
rows.anchor: وَقَالَ صَوَابًۭا o izne nâil olabileceklerin sıfat-ı kâşifesini ve şefaatin birinci şartını beyan olmasıdır.

rows.speaker: birtakım müfessirîn
rows.claim: An alternative takes the exception as the people for whom intercession is made; “spoke correctly” means they had uttered the testimony of divine unity in worldly life, so sinful believers may eventually receive intercession through their faith.
rows.anchor: Yani “Rahmân’ın izin verdiği ve dünyada bir savab söylemiş olan kimseler hakkında söylemeleri ve şefaat etmeleri müstesnâ” demek olur ki birtakım müfessirîn buna kāil olmuşlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı cites a Prophetic hadith promising intercession for major sinners of the Prophet’s community as support for eventual intercession for sinful believers.
rows.anchor: شَفَاعَتِي لأَِهْلِ الْكَبَائِرِ مِنْ أُمَّتِي hadîs-i şerîfi[^13] mûcebince

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm tarjuju is accusative as an adverb of time connected to the omitted answer of the oath: resurrection will occur on that day.
rows.anchor: Kasemin mahzuf olan cevâbına müte‘allik mef‘ûl-i fîh olarak mansubdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajf can be transitive or intransitive, meaning either to shake violently or to be violently shaken; the Rājifah may therefore be the first trumpet blast or the earth and mountains that shake.
rows.anchor: “Recf” şiddetle sarsmak veya sarsılmak mânasına müte‘addî ve lâzım olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transitive sense is more emphatic: the first blast violently mobilizes the world.
rows.anchor: Evvelki ta‘diye mânası tehvilde eblağdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Rādifah follows the first blast and may include continuing movements such as the sky splitting and stars scattering, but the second trumpet blast is more likely and fits the context.
rows.anchor: ilk nefha da zelzelenin tevâlîsi gibi harekâtın tevâlîsini, semânın inşikākı ve kevâkibin intişârı hâllerini de ifade etmiş olabilirse de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “day” means the interval extending from the first shaking until resurrection.
rows.anchor: Demek ki “gün”den murad, reciften ba‘se kadar mümted olan vakittir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the resurrection is asserted with oath and emphasis, the passage recounts what deniers say in this world.
rows.anchor: Ba‘sin vukū‘u kasem ve tekid ile haber verildikten sonra ba‘si inkâr eden münkirlerin sözlerini hikâyedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāfirah originally describes something that digs, then came to mean a horse’s hoof, its track, and the groove it digs.
rows.anchor: “Hâfir,[^1] Hâfire” esasen kazıcı mânasına sıfat olmakla beraber atın tırnağına isim olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom rujūʿ fī al-hāfirah means returning along one’s former route; the verse uses it figuratively for being restored to the former life and creation.
rows.anchor: رُجُوع فِي الْحَافِرَة geldiği yolda dönmekten kinâye olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another idiom, naqd fī al-hāfirah, means paying cash immediately in a transaction; Elmalılı records competing explanations for the horse-hoof image behind it.
rows.anchor: نقد في الحافره denilir ki, bir alışverişte müşterinin ilk sözde parayı sayması mânasında kullanılır.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas’s reported and exegetically preferred reading takes hāfirah as a figurative return to the prior state of life and creation.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas Hazretleri’nden mervî ve müfessirînin muhtârıdır.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also reports hāfirah as the grave, like a dug-out pit; Elmalılı finds the grave rendering clearer, though less apparent, and says both readings converge.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den “hâfire” “hufre” gibi mahfûre, yani kazılan çukur yer mânasına olarak kabir diye de rivayet edilmiş olduğu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the grave sense is less apparent, Elmalılı favors translating “that pit” because it is clearer and mardudun already implies return; both interpretations mean resurrection after death.
rows.anchor: bu mâna herkese daha vâzıh geleceği için “o hufre” demeyi münasib gördük

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nakhirah can mean decayed bones crumbling and blowing away, or perforated bones that whistle in the wind; the forms nehire and nahire can distinguish these senses.
rows.anchor: “Nehire” çürümüş ufalanmış, rüzgârla savrulur, yahut delik deşik göz göz olmuş, rüzgâr estikçe ses verir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers infer that dead bones cannot be revived, echoing 36:78; Elmalılı calls this incredulity and denial.
rows.anchor: مَن يُحْىِ ٱلْعِظَٰمَ وَهِىَ رَمِيمٌۭ [36/78] demeleri gibi istib‘âd ve inkâr ettiler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that resurrection would be a ruinous return is mockery: they expect loss because they did not believe or prepare for it.
rows.anchor: Çünkü o denildiği gibi ise biz ona iman etmemiş, hazırlanmamış olduğumuz için bize çok hüsran verecek bir dönüş olacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers that resurrection is no difficult matter: it takes only one commanding cry, accomplished by the command kun.
rows.anchor: onu Allah’a göre zor bir şey zannetmeyin, o bir tek zecirden, zorlu bir kumanda ile bir sayhadan ibarettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Immediately after that single blast, they find themselves on the Sāhirah.
rows.anchor: derhâl onlar sâhirede bulunurlar.
